D_800C7A78.title: Native frame-submission counter
D_800C7A78.summary: Unsigned 16-bit frame counter whose parity drives the native player hurt-recovery flicker.
behavior: A live unsigned 16-bit counter at g_system +0x3ADB8. The exact exported symbol has no ROM suffix.
The native frame-submission routine at 0x8000098C increments this counter when it submits a prepared frame. It wraps at the width of the stored halfword.

The player recovery updater reads this counter with LHU. While player task byte +0xD4 is nonzero, it writes object byte +0x64 = counter & 1: even parity is visible and odd parity hides rendering. When the timer reaches zero it forces the object visible.
The kind-2 model renderer checks object +0x64 bit 0 before drawing. That render flag does not remove the task, change its model or scale, or disable its collision body.
D_800C7A78.exampleExplanation: Updates only the native render-hide bit, preserving the remaining object state. The original player recovery updater also manages invulnerability and its countdown; this visual helper does not replace that gameplay behavior.
cautions: This is a native frame counter, not elapsed seconds or a timestamp. Its phase is local to one running game.
Do not simulate flicker by deleting or unbinding an actor, setting its scale to zero, or disabling collision. Native flicker changes the render flag only.
Read the halfword at its exact width. A word access would include neighboring native state.

func_80034A10_35610.title: Reset native task storage
func_80034A10_35610.summary: Clears native task linkage, callback, object, contact and common work fields before storage is reused.
behavior: Receives a task-storage pointer and returns the same pointer. Clears links at +0x00/+0x04, callbacks, primary and secondary object pointers, contact state and the common task work range.
The native allocator at 0x80034B58 calls this resetter after taking a task from the free pool and before writing its new linkage, priority and callback.
An entry hook can discard cached external identities associated with the task address before the new task lifetime begins. Address equality alone cannot distinguish old and newly allocated tasks.
func_80034A10_35610.exampleExplanation: The hook invalidates a caller-owned cached identity and leaves native reset/allocation behavior untouched.
cautions: This is a storage resetter, not a safe destructor for a linked task. Calling it directly on a live actor erases pointers without performing its complete destruction lifecycle.
At an entry hook, fields still belong to the preceding storage state; they do not describe the new object that the allocator has not constructed yet.
The same task and object addresses can be reused within one frame. Use lifecycle observation when assigning a durable external identity.

D_8020D220_5C9130.title: Reusable player broad-resource buffer
D_8020D220_5C9130.summary: Native pointer storage for the current player's reusable broad-character resource buffer.
behavior: The native resource initializer at 0x801DC630 reserves 0x18000 bytes from the scene resource arena and writes the buffer pointer at entry 0. The inspected initializer establishes only this one entry.

The character-resource loader at 0x801DC9C8 indexes this storage using the playable task's byte at +0x90, loads the broad file selected by D_80204020_5BFF30[character], and checks that its returned end pointer stays within the reserved 0x18000 bytes.
Player-owned visual constructors can bind this buffer as their broad-resource segment. It holds the currently loaded character data and can be overwritten during a character change.
D_8020D220_5C9130.exampleExplanation: Returns the single buffer entry established by the inspected initializer. The pointer does not grant ownership of the resource arena.
cautions: This is pointer storage, not the beginning of the character file itself. Dereference entry 0 to obtain the buffer.
Only index 0 is established by the inspected initialization. Do not infer a four-character array or independent buffers from native indexed syntax.
The address also appears in another overlay with a different ROM suffix. Preserve the complete _5C9130 symbol identity.
A cached pointer can remain numerically equal while its character contents change. Resolve its resource identity and lifecycle before retaining a visual reference.
